text:
Priya (support): Hey team, getting a 502 spike from edge in us-west-2 right after the canary deploy ~12:45 PST. ~2.8% of requests for hostedapi are failing. Sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d
Alex (eng-runtime): thanks — any repro steps? can you paste a curl?
Priya (support): curl repro attached: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt": "hello"}'`
Priya (support): logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `502 no healthy upstream` coming from frontdoor NGINX.
Ben (eng-sre): ops-bot just flagged a host eviction event on edgenet-37 in the same AZ at 12:43. Could be transient.
ops-bot: [alert] host evicted edgenet-37 -> drain triggered, 12:43:09
Dara (oncall): I see a pattern: burst of auth header rotations from billing service coinciding with the eviction. Large header size from billing caused conn resets?
Alex (eng-runtime): hmm if billing service is sending long headers it can exhaust accept queue and trigger 502s at the nginx front. Any 502 body?
Priya (support): 502 body from nginx: `{"error": "upstream temporally unavailable"}`. We also have a few HTTP/2 RST_STREAM logs.
Liam (product): customer says latency increased for small chat calls too, not only big embeddings. Could be routing fallback to warm hosts.
Ben (eng-sre): Rolling back the canary would help isolate. Can we confirm if the new config changed `keepalive_timeout` or large header buffering?
Alex (eng-runtime): I pushed a quick probe to compare two variants: old `keepalive_timeout: 75s` vs new `60s`. Also checking `client_header_buffer_size` and `large_client_header_buffers`.
Priya (support): Updated ticket with sample request ids: [req: 0x9f3a, 0x9f3b, 0x9f3c]. Customers seeing ~10x error rate for tenant `acme-inc` during 12:43-12:52.
Dara (oncall): mitigation: temporarily disable the canary in us-west-2 and fail open to dedicated pool. Initiating rollback now.
Ben (eng-sre): rolling back canary — will monitor 1m buckets.
ops-bot: rollback completed for canary-deploy-2026-03-18-12-40, 12:50:03
Alex (eng-runtime): post-rollback metrics show 502s dropped to baseline within 90s. Correlation strong with canary + host eviction + billing-header spike.
Priya (support): customer notified, asked to confirm they see improvement. leaving notes for follow-up: increase `large_client_header_buffers` and add a deploy-time check for header size from internal billing calls.
Liam (product): we'll add a post-deploy canary healthcheck that includes auth header fuzzing.
Alex (eng-runtime): opened infra ticket to harden edgenet host draining and add backpressure on billing gateway. ticket: INF-4321
Priya (support): thanks all — closing incident once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
